'''Jochen Heisenberg''' (born 16 May 1939) is a German physicist specializing in [[nuclear physics]], and Professor Emeritus of Physics at the [[University of New Hampshire]]. He is the son of [[Nobel Prize]]-winning physicist [[Werner Heisenberg]], who was a co-founder of [[quantum mechanics]], and who, in particular, introduced the [[uncertainty principle]]. He is the brother of [[Germany|German]] [[neurobiologist]] and [[geneticist]] [[Martin Heisenberg]] and the uncle of film director [[Benjamin Heisenberg]].

==Professional career==
Heisenberg studied physics first at [[LMU Munich]], and then finished his <span lang="de" dir="ltr">''[[Diplom]]''</span> at the [[University of Hamburg]], where he continued his studies with [[Willibald Jentschke]] and received his PhD in 1968. He then spent a two-year postdoctoral fellowship at [[Stanford University]]. From 1970 to 1978, he was a member of the faculty at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].

During his early career at Stanford and MIT, Heisenberg participated in numerous experimental studies of nuclear reactions. Using the Bates Linear Accelerator, he published numerous papers on electroexcitations.<ref>
{{cite journal
 | title= High multipolarity electroexcitations in 207Pb and 206Pb
 | author= Papanicolas
 | journal= Physics Letters B
 | volume= 99
 | issue= 2
 | pages= 96–100
 | year= 1981
 | publisher= Elsevier
 | doi= 10.1016/0370-2693(81)90958-8
|bibcode = 1981PhLB...99...96P |first=CN|last2=Heisenberg|first2=J.|last3=Lichtenstadt|first3=J.|last4=McCarthy|first4=JS}}
</ref> After his move to the [[University of New Hampshire]] (UNH), he began to study methods for theoretical prediction of such reactions. During the past ten years,{{when|date=December 2023}} he has been active in the development of computational models of large nuclei and has published several papers on these topics.<ref>
{{cite journal
 | title=Ground state correlations and mean field in <sup>16</sup>O. II. Effects of a three-nucleon interaction
 |author1=Mihaila, B.  |author2=Heisenberg, J.H.
 | journal= Physical Review C
 | volume= 61
 | issue= 5
 | article-number= 54309
 | year= 2000
 | publisher= APS
 | doi= 10.1103/PhysRevC.61.054309
|arxiv = nucl-th/9912023 |bibcode = 2000PhRvC..61e4309M |s2cid=119081245 }}
</ref>

==Historical perspectives==
Heisenberg has spoken several times to provide a historical perspective on the activities of his father during and after World War II. He has been invited to comment on [[Michael Frayn]]'s well-known play ''[[Copenhagen (play)|Copenhagen]]''<ref>
{{cite journal
 | title= Frayn's "Heisenberg": Fact or fiction?
 | author= Heisenberg, J.
 | journal= Resonance
 | volume= 9
 | issue= 8
 | pages= 90–98
 | year= 2004
 | publisher= Springer
 | doi= 10.1007/BF02837584
| s2cid= 121033659
 }}
</ref> and has published his perspectives on his father's activities.<ref><nowiki>
</nowiki>{{cite journal
 | title= Personal Reflections
 | author= Heisenberg, J.
 | journal= Resonance
 | volume= 10
 | issue= 1
 | pages= 93–96
 | year= 2005
 | publisher= Springer
 | doi= 10.1007/BF02835899
| s2cid= 26665559
 }}
</ref> He maintained an [https://web.archive.org/web/20180809172620/http://heisenbergfamily.org/ informational website] containing biographical information and reference material on [[Werner Heisenberg]].
